While maps form vital pieces of military planning, operations, and assessment a different application arose during the latter part of the Second World War. Known as service unit maps, unit route maps, pictorial maps, or triumphal maps, maps like these were produced to maintain and convey units’ experiences of their services and routes across the North African, European, and Pacific theaters. Undoubtably, there was also an aspect of maintaining or boosting morale and sense of purpose.
